body:
Parent: #35. Related: #5, #8, #15.

## Decision to enable
Which host/backend profiles can V0 realistically support, and which assumptions must be resolved before designing production backend abstractions? Do not assume rootless Intel, nested-vPMU support, a common progress/time implementation, or cross-backend equality.

## First bounded investigation
- Inventory the available NixOS workstation and existing relevant evidence without changing host configuration.
- Define and, where a second accessible authorized Zen host exists, execute a same-artifact cross-host replay matrix. If unavailable, report the resource blocker immediately; still deliver the reproducible procedure.
- Investigate Intel KVM event/guest-only counting/overflow availability, skid behavior, privilege requirements and nested-vPMU exposure using primary documentation and executable probes on available authorized hardware.
- Assess the existing Mac TCG experiment against independent machines, PV time ABI, exact deterministic replay and production integration needs. Preserve distinctions between scoped observation hashes and execution/full-state evidence.
- Build a capability/uncertainty matrix: demonstrated within scope, disproven, unresolved, next experiment and decision consequence.

## Boundaries
Research only; no production backend abstraction or backend implementation. Keep probes/raw results on a dedicated experiment branch or isolated artifact paths; write conclusions in this issue. No cloud provisioning/purchases. No sweeping host changes. Coordinate guest runs with the engine owner, who has priority.
Initial budget: two elapsed hours of investigation and at most one allocated core-hour of guest execution before a checkpoint, stopping earlier on decisive findings or missing hardware. No retries without a stated hypothesis.

## Acceptance
Deliver tested or executable qualification procedures with pinned artifacts and host/profile inventory; identify replay compatibility gates and immediate design decisions. A documented missing resource is a valid blocked research result, not evidence of support. Submit the findings to Astra for challenge review; bring decisions back to manager before downstream implementation.
Sol 6.1 Max. Follow #35's same-version determinism rule, evidence and coordination policies.
title: M1 research: qualify replay profiles and bound Intel/TCG feasibility

body:
## Objective
Coordinate the first Seedbox V0 batch against vision #25. V0 covers M0–M4: a new user runs a real application, finds and groups a failure, exports it, and a colleague replays the recorded execution with MATCH on a compatible qualified profile.

## Non-negotiable contract
For the same application and Seedbox versions, seed, retained inputs, and compatible qualified execution profile, execution must reproduce exactly. Different software versions may legitimately execute differently. Within a version, performance-only settings and observation must not change execution. Unexplained divergence blocks acceptance; re-pinning is not a substitute for diagnosis.

One VM per service remains the reference/default KVM layout per #34. Cross-backend equality is research, not an assumed V0 guarantee.

## First batch
- Engine reliability: #33 plus default-margin/undo PMU failures, owned together.
- Acceptance migration: reconcile #27 and identify remaining legacy consumers; engine semantics changes belong to the engine owner.
- Backend qualification research: second-Zen qualification procedure and Intel/TCG feasibility; related #5, #8, #15.
- Scenario contract design: verdicts, outputs, random streams, histories/checkers, and controller/workload boundary. Design before M2 implementation.
- One independent Astra High reviewer, with early design review for risky work.

Child issue links, chat ownership, and status will be added in a follow-up comment.

## Decision gates
Each lane states prerequisites, useful work possible now, its stopping point before an unproven assumption, a bounded experiment, and how each outcome changes the plan. Research outcomes are demonstrated within scope, disproven, or unresolved. An unresolved outcome does not unlock dependent implementation.
- Engine: reproduce and identify causes, review semantic correction before implementation, then qualify candidate and pin evidence.
- Acceptance: portable migration can advance; hardware acceptance and removal of legacy coverage wait for evidence.
- Backends: retain probes and profile inventories; no production architecture or portability claim before qualification.
- Scenarios: agree on public behavior and contracts before implementing M2.
Record throughput/boot/memory costs opportunistically so snapshots can move ahead of V0 if evidence requires it.

## Review and management
The manager reads issues, reports and evidence summaries, not source or diffs. Implementation workers are Sol 6.1 High/Max; reviewer is Astra High and performs no coding.
Workers and reviewer iterate directly. When final review is ready, the reviewer first sends only the issue and exact PR revision to the manager, withholding implementation details and recommendation. The manager independently states expected high-level behavior from agreed requirements. The reviewer then explains the actual correspondence, gaps and supporting evidence, including a one-paragraph quality judgement. Manager acceptance is required before final reviewer OK. Approval is revision-specific. No merges are authorized by this batch kickoff.
If assumptions fail or scope drifts, freeze affected work and surface the decision; independent work may continue.

## Evidence and resources
Use issues for findings and decision records; retain raw artifacts/probes on dedicated experiment branches or isolated workstation paths and link them. Do not put experiment narratives into production source. Production regression tests and reusable qualification tools may be reviewed normally.
The user authorizes code execution and data transfer to/from the NixOS workstation without additional permission. Use project Nix environments, isolated checkouts/output, shared CPU/SMT leases, exact MSR restoration, bounded jobs and resource coordination. Never disturb unrelated jobs/state or managed GitHub credentials.
Engine reliability gets priority for scarce qualification capacity. Other lanes inspect availability and coordinate before campaigns. Initial exploration budget: at most two elapsed hours of investigation and one allocated core-hour of guest execution per research lane before reporting findings/remaining unknowns; stop earlier at a decisive result. Do not provision paid infrastructure without a separate decision.

## Completion of the batch
Each lane produces its agreed deliverable or a precise blocked/unresolved report, with evidence and proposed next decision. Reevaluate dependencies, scope, review throughput and experiment cost before expanding concurrency.

## Batch dispatched
| Lane | Issue | Model | First checkpoint |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Engine reliability | #33 | Sol 6.1 Max | Reproductions, causal diagnosis, proposed semantic correction and qualification matrix |
| Public-CLI acceptance migration | #36, continuing #27 | Sol 6.1 High | Consumer/coverage inventory and conflict/dependency assessment |
| Backend qualification research | #37 | Sol 6.1 Max | Hardware availability, falsifiable probes and capability/uncertainty matrix |
| Scenario contract design | #38 | Sol 6.1 High | Two developer examples, contracts and unresolved decisions |
| Independent review | This issue | Astra High | Early design challenge, then revision-specific independent expectation gate |

All five dedicated Codex chats are created and have the roster and direct coordination authorization. The manager remains outside code/diff review.

Engine owner owns the integrated candidate qualification proposal. Genuine historical failing-workload coverage must remain distinct from planted checker controls. Missing second-host/Intel hardware produces an explicit blocker and executable protocol, not a support claim. Scenario outcomes and deterministic versus host-cost outputs are design questions to settle before M2 implementation.

Initial concurrency policy: no more than one guest job per lane until coordinated allocation, exclusive CPU/SMT leases, bounded builds, isolated state/artifacts, and engine priority for scarce hardware. First research/diagnostic checkpoint is within two elapsed hours and one allocated core-hour of guest execution, or sooner on decisive findings/blockers. Workers must report before continuing beyond those bounds.

No merges are part of kickoff. Final reviewer readiness is blind to manager expectations; design-only gates use a stable issue-comment/design revision in place of a PR SHA.

title: V0 batch 1: stabilization, qualification, and scenario contracts
